title: NaturopathyClear
question: How does naturopathy work?
hook: Hip baths, mud packs, fasting and sunshine: naturopathy heals without medicines, and Gandhi was its biggest fan. Walk its 200-year story from a Silesian water cure to Urulikanchan, see its five-element model as it tells it, then watch what hot water, cold water and a 3-day fast really do inside you, and where the evidence stands.

explainer.title: From water cure to village ashram
explainer.text: Nature cure began with Priessnitz's cold-water spa (1822), Kneipp's My Water Cure (1886) and Kuhne's 'one disease, one cure' (1891). Kuhne reached India in Telugu around 1894. Gandhi championed it, wrote Key to Health and opened a village ashram at Urulikanchan in 1946. Today it is the N in AYUSH, with CCRYN (1978), NIN Pune (1986), the BNYS degree and Naturopathy Day on 18 November.

explainer.title: Five elements, as naturopathy tells it
explainer.text: Naturopathy pairs the five elements with therapies: space with fasting, air with air baths and pranayama, fire with sun baths, water with hydrotherapy, earth with mud and diet. It holds that the body heals itself once 'foreign matter' is cleared through skin, lungs, kidneys and bowels. That load is an idea, not something a lab measures.

explainer.title: What water really does
explainer.text: Cold water narrows skin blood vessels and hot water opens them wide. Because flow grows with the radius to the fourth power, a vessel 1.6 times wider carries about 7 times the blood. A hip bath moves tens of watts of heat, but your core barely changes. Below about 15 °C, a full plunge triggers cold shock.

explainer.title: Where it meets good science
explainer.text: Healthy-living parts hold up. In trials of people with high blood pressure, brisk exercise lowers the top number by about 8 mmHg, less salt by about 5 and a plant-rich plate by about 11. Yoga helps by about 4, with weaker studies. ICMR-NIN's 2024 guidelines say at most 5 g of salt a day.

explainer.title: Fair tests, fasting and detox
explainer.text: In a fast the liver's sugar store runs low within a day, then new glucose and ketones keep a healthy adult steady. On insulin, or in pregnancy, fasting can be dangerous. Your kidneys already filter about 180 litres of plasma a day; no good trial shows detox diets remove toxins.

explainer.title: Using it wisely
explainer.text: Keep the good habits: sleep, daily movement, vegetables, less salt and sugar, fresh air and calm. Use nature cure alongside medicine, never instead of it for serious illness, and never stop insulin, blood-pressure or other prescribed medicines. Chest pain, stroke signs or fainting need a qualified doctor now.

concepts.def: A drug-free system of healing that uses diet, fasting, water, mud, sun, air, massage and exercise.
The five great elements, space, air, fire, water and earth, that naturopathy says make up the body.
'The healing power of nature': the belief that the body tends to heal itself.
Treatment with water at different temperatures, such as hip baths, foot baths, packs and steam.
Blood vessels widening, which sends more blood to the skin, as in a hot bath.
The liver making new glucose during a fast, once its glycogen store runs low.
Fuels the liver makes from fat when food is scarce; the brain can use them.
Feeling better because you expect to, which is why fair tests compare against a control group.
Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences, India's 5½-year degree in naturopathy and yoga.
